# The Field Guide
This feature is: [color=orange]In-Progress[/color].
## Anvils & You
In order to use an anvil, you must first have two things on you. Firstly, metal(s) to put in it's internal storage, and a hammer in any of your hands (doesn't have to be the active hand).
Once you have those, you are ready to start smithing. Follow these steps:
1. Insert your desired metal into the anvil. You can do that by clicking on it, or via the context menu verb. 2. Hold the hammer in your active hand, and right click the anvil to open the context menu. Click "Toggle UI" to open the anvil UI. 2.5. From this point, you can have your hammer in any hand. 3. You'll notice there's a few slots at the top of the UI, and a button called "Outputs". Clicking on the button will show the recipes available for those metals you put in before. 4. Once you open the recipes menu, you may click on a recipe of your choice, and click the button at the bottom to confirm your choice. 5. You may now begin the minigame.
## How to complete a recipe
The minigame of the anvil is simple, but requires memorization and simple math. Here's how it works: - There's two progress bars. One green, and one red. Both have a value displayed inside of them. - The green bar indicates your progress. Your goal is to meet the red bar's value. - The red bar indicates the work required for the recipe to complete itself. - On the left and right you may see grids of numbers, positive and negative respectively. Those are called "hit numbers". - If you click on a positive number, the green bar will go up, otherwise it will go down with a negative number. - This is basically it. Click the right combination of numbers to match the green bar with the red bar.
Once a recipe is complete, the result will spawn on top of the anvil, and the metals will no longer appear in the UI or storage.
Although this sounds simple for most recipes, advanced ones have an extra layer of difficulty called "Patterns"
A pattern is a sequence of numbers you must meet before the recipe is considered complete. As an example, if a recipe has a pattern with these numbers: - 7, 5, -5
And the required work for the recipe is 60, then you'd have to hit 7, 5, -5 in the exact order, and the last number of that pattern sequence should lead to 60.
If you hit the pattern, and the last number doesn't lead to the work required, then the pattern will reset.
## What is next for Anvils?
The anvils are obviously too simple now, even with patterns.
There's 2 features that will affect anvils in the future. - Heating/Cooling metals. Metals will need to be above a certain temp. in order to be workable. The blacksmith must be quick with working. - Flux. It will be a required material for working on metals. - More recipes. - Durability for the hammer, along with special hammer effects.
